newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia's Cilacap 200,000-bpd CDU to shut in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Cilacap 200,000-bpd CDU to shut in Oct.

text.p: Indonesian state-owned Pertamina plans to shut its 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) at the Cilacap refinery from early October for up to three months for maintenance and upgrading works, company sources said on Tuesday.
"The shutdown will allow for debottlenecking works to be done and to link CDU-2 with lube unit number three," a source said.
The Cilacap complex now has two lube base oil plants with a total production capacity of 250,000 tonnes per year (tpy).
The third lube unit will raise the capacity to 428,000 tpy when construction works are completed as scheduled by the end of 1998, sources said.
A 100,000-bpd CDU at Cilacap is also undergoing a scheduled 35-day maintenance since August 12.

Industry sources said the upgrading works will also allow Pertamina to boost the refining capacity at CDU-1 to 118,000 bpd from 100,000 bpd, and at CDU-2 to 230,000 bpd from 200,000 bpd by the end of 1998.
The expansion project involved investments amounting to US$630 million with the financing agreement being lead-arranged by U.S. bank Citicorp , industry sources said.
Under the deal, Royal Dutch Shell would guarantee to lift one 70,000-to-80,000-tonne cargo of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) and one 25,000-to-30,000-tonne cargo of naphtha per month, they said.
The extended shutdown period of CDU-2 is also to allow Pertamina to integrate the crude units with newly built storage tanks to replace damaged ones, industry source said.
Seven oil product storage tanks were damaged in a fire in end-October 1995 after being hit by lightning.
The Cilacap complex, which is located 290 km (180 miles) from the capital Jakarta, is the biggest oil refinery in Indonesia, producing one-third of the country's refined products.
